sampling_model.design: Independent uniform complete randomization on \(B\) and \(S\), with exactly \(n_B\) treated buyers and \(n_S\) treated sellers.
sampling_model.units: The finite populations \(B\) and \(S\) and all dyad potential outcomes are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: A dyad has exposure \((z_i^B,z_j^S)\in\{0,1\}^2\); the tested contrast compares \((1,1)\) with \((0,0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No superpopulation overlap condition is used; positivity is the finite support condition \(h(a,b)\ge R\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. The procedure enumerates or exactly samples the conditional randomization law.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 establishes validity of Procedure 3.2 for any equal block size \(k\); within that published equal-square family the retained focal count is \(2nk\).
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: At \(R=4\), thm:strict-equal-block-delta proves the exact published-subclass optimum \(\Phi_n^{\mathrm{eq}}(4)=2n^2/\ell(n)\), where \(\ell(n)\) is the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, and compares it with the exact covering paired-rectangle frontier. Even \(n\) gives the sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope, while prime \(n\) gives ratio \(n-2+2/n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The randomization test described in Procedure 1 is valid conditionally at any level.
If \(T\) is imputable, the randomization test is valid at any level \(\alpha\).
Then, \(W\) is uniformly distributed conditional on the event \(\{W\in\mathcal B\}\).
If \(T\) is effect increasing, then \(p^{L+}(D^{\mathrm{obs}},\theta)\) is non-decreasing in \(\theta\).
The concentration probability is maximized when all the \(a_i\) are \(\pm1\).

body.tldr: For independently and uniformly half-randomized populations on two unequal market sides, the optimal covering rectangle at required support \(R\) reduces to a finite residual catalog depending only on \(R\). For \(R\ge4\) and \(n_B,n_S\ge4R\), the exact frontier is the maximum of finitely many affine catalog scores and every tie is retained. On balanced squares at \(R=4\), if \(\ell(n)\) is the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, then the published equal-square optimum is exactly \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), while the covering paired-rectangle optimum is \(2(n-1)^2+2\). Their exact ratio is \(\ell(n)(1-2/n+2/n^2)\): even sizes form the sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope, whereas prime sizes have ratio \(n-2+2/n\). A constant-incidence sampler implements the selected event, and null-adjusted focal outcomes yield exact one-sided inversion for a sharp constant total effect. No universal collapse of the catalog to diagonal unit residuals is claimed.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact two-sided-market method proves validity for selected equal blocks and treats block choice within that published equal-square subclass; it neither identifies the support-four optimum \(2n^2/\ell(n)\) from the least nontrivial divisor nor optimizes over unequal covering rectangles. General biclique methods establish validity and power guidance but do not classify the optimal covering paired rectangle. Marketplace bias-and-variance analyses motivate the design problem but do not solve this exact rectangle optimization, and existing one-dimensional subset-sum purification does not preserve a prescribed common buyer--seller target fiber.
project_justification.niche: Balanced independent randomization converts admissible covering rectangles into two coupled half-sum profiles. This structure permits an exact finite residual reduction and affine phase analysis for unequal market-side sizes. On the balanced \(R=4\) slice it also yields an exact arithmetic classification of the published equal-square benchmark through \(\ell(n)\), the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, without asserting an unrestricted-biclique optimum.
project_justification.fill: A two-stage concentration argument bounds the residual on the smaller side and uses a support-preserving residual-copy comparison to bound the larger residual. This yields a finite catalog and an exact affine frontier with all catalog ties. At \(R=4\), every proper equal-block divisor is eligible, so the published equal-square optimum is exactly \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), versus the covering paired-rectangle value \(2(n-1)^2+2\). The exact ratio \(\ell(n)(1-2/n+2/n^2)\) has its sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope on even sizes and equals \(n-2+2/n\) at prime sizes. The same catalog supports an implementable conditional law and exact one-sided sharp-null inversion. Whether every catalog entry can be purified to a dominating diagonal unit-residual entry remains a separate open question.

body.related_work: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026) establish the equal \(k\)-block total-effect test and motivate the support--focal-size trade-off. Within their published equal-square subclass, the present result proves that the exact support-four optimum is \(\Phi_n^{\mathrm{eq}}(4)=2n^2/\ell(n)\), with \(\ell(n)\) the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, and compares it with the exact covering paired-rectangle optimum \(2(n-1)^2+2\). Even sizes give the sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope, while prime sizes give ratio \(n-2+2/n\). Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022) encode imputable tests as bicliques and motivate large bicliques, but do not supply the paired-rectangle classification. Li, Zhao, Johari, and Weintraub (2021) study interference-induced bias and variance in two-sided marketplace experiments, and Johari, Li, Liskovich, and Weintraub (2022) analyze bias under two-sided platform designs; both motivate why focal retention and design choice matter, but neither is a competing exact covering-rectangle optimization result. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) provide the conditioning-mechanism validity theorem used after imputability is verified. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024) provide the orbit-equivariance template, while unequal rectangular profiles require a separate constant-incidence count. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021) provide discrete Fisher inversion machinery, specialized here after null-adjusted dyadic imputability and crossing monotonicity are established. Singhal (2019) motivates bilinear subset-sum profiles and one-dimensional purification, but does not furnish a coupled common-fiber-preserving reduction to diagonal unit residuals. Ye et al. (2023) provide the unequal-side marketplace consumer through Platform O's independent user-view and ad randomizations.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The conditioning event must be selected without outcomes. Raw focal outcomes are not imputable under a nonzero sharp constant effect, so the null-adjusted array \(Q_\tau\) is essential. Complement symmetry implies that an ordinary nonrandomized absolute-score test has minimum \(p\)-value at least \(2/h(a,b)\), so support \(20\) cannot support an ordinary two-sided test at level \(0.05\). In addition, the finite catalog has not been proved to collapse universally to the diagonal unit-residual subcatalog: known one-dimensional purification arguments do not preserve the required joint buyer--seller target fiber.
body.honest_scope: The note proves the finite residual catalog, exact affine frontier and catalog equality cases, the constant-incidence sampler, and exact one-sided inversion under the sharp constant total-effect null. On balanced squares at \(R=4\), it also proves the exact published equal-square comparator formula \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), the exact gap and ratio against the covering paired-rectangle optimum, the sharp even-size factor-two asymptotic lower envelope, and the prime-size ratio \(n-2+2/n\). Universal unit-residual purification remains an explicit unresolved question and is not used by those results. The note makes no claim about weak-null validity, power or confidence-width optimality, unrestricted bicliques, minimality of the \(4R\) threshold, ordinary two-sided \(95\)-percent inversion at support \(20\), or the empirical validity of the constant-effect exposure model for Platform O.
body.interpretation: The finite-catalog result is the actionable design certificate: for fixed resolution \(R\), one enumerates \(\mathcal C_R\), evaluates the affine scores at the two market sizes, and retains every maximizer on a phase boundary. The balanced-square \(R=4\) slice has a complete arithmetic comparator: letting \(\ell(n)\) be the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, the best published equal-square profile retains \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), while the optimal covering paired rectangle retains \(2(n-1)^2+2\). The exact ratio is \(\ell(n)(1-2/n+2/n^2)\). Even sizes, for which \(\ell(n)=2\), attain the sharp lower envelope \(2-4/n+4/n^2\) and establish limit inferior two; prime sizes, for which \(\ell(n)=n\), have ratio \(n-2+2/n\) and therefore a linear-scale separation. These comparisons concern the published equal-square subclass, not unrestricted bicliques. The unresolved unit-residual question concerns only whether the already finite computation admits a further universal closed-form collapse; it is not needed for catalog optimality, this exact comparison, sampling, or exact one-sided inversion.
